problem: Outdoor long-range navigation typically depends on accurate, costly-to-maintain global maps, and existing trajectory generators use only one or two modalities (geometry, color, or language), giving incomplete scene understanding for traversability and social compliance.
motivation: Humans navigate long distances with only coarse map routing (e.g. Google Maps), so a robot could split navigation into GPS/QGIS routing plus local trajectory generation. Geometry fails when terrains have similar elevation (mud vs sidewalk), segmentation fails out-of-distribution, and social norms need common sense, so fusing complementary modalities is needed.
key_idea: Decompose global navigation into GPS routing with sparse subgoals plus local trajectory generation that scores CVAE-generated LiDAR trajectories by fusing geometric confidence, image semantic traversability, VLM social ranking and GPS-goal distance.
insight: The modalities have complementary failure modes: the LiDAR CVAE fails when off-road and sidewalk have similar elevation, and Mask2Former fails on out-of-distribution ground and misses curbs, so a weighted sum is more robust. On GND the full fusion reaches 77% traversability vs 65% for VL-TGS (Points+RGB+Language) and 61% for geometry-only MTG, though no component-wise ablation table is given. The VLM adds most of the latency (2.30 s).
method: Routing: public routing services (Google/OpenRoute) with QGIS/GPS yield GPS subgoals spaced ~50 m apart (GPS error ~5 m); switch to the next subgoal within 10 m.
CVAE trajectory generation (MTG): PointCNN on LiDAR plus velocity history encoders produce N candidate trajectories via a CVAE; latent variance gives a geometric confidence score c.

Semantic traversability: Mask2Former segments RGB into 5 classes (road, sidewalk, vegetation, building, others); wheeled robots may only use road/sidewalk; trajectories are rasterized with Bresenham and scored by the fraction of traversable pixels t.

VLM ranking: trajectories are overlaid and numbered on the image with a prompt about pedestrians, traffic rules, crosswalks, signs and off-road; Gemini outputs robot mode (normal/slow), ranking and reasoning; rank score r=(N-p)/N.
Score fusion: choose argmax of β1 c + β2 t + β3 r + β4 g (g = closeness to GPS subgoal), aggregated over multiple consecutive frames transformed into the current frame.
Motion planning: DWA follows the chosen trajectory; the VLM velocity mode caps max speed (1 m/s normal, <0.5 m/s slow).

setting.backbone: MTG CVAE with PointCNN (trained) + Mask2Former (pretrained) + Gemini (frozen VLM) + DWA
setting.training_data: Reuses pretrained MTG/Mask2Former and frozen Gemini; no new training data reported (GND dataset used for evaluation)
setting.observation: 3D LiDAR point clouds, monocular RGB, robot velocity/odometry, GPS
setting.action_space: local trajectories executed by DWA velocity commands (max 1 m/s, slow <0.5 m/s)
setting.simulator: none (GND real-world dataset; real-world on-road tests)
setting.privileged: none (GPS + public routing map; GT traversability map used only for metric on GND)

results: On GND, MOSU achieves 77% traversability and 73% distance-to-target, vs VL-TGS 65/70, DTG 67/66, PIVOT 70/69, MTG 61/64. Claims at least ~10% higher traversability than others with comparable distance, at 2.30 s inference dominated by the VLM.
limitations: VLM inference is slow (2.3 s), limiting real-time use
Cannot detect small cliffs such as vertical ramp surfaces
Learning-based components generalize poorly out-of-distribution, yielding noisy trajectories; no component ablation or real-world quantitative table
